17	# LaTeX 论文写作全流程
18	
19	ML/AI 顶会论文从草稿到投稿的完整指南。整合 Orchestra Research、VibeSkills、claim2evidence 三方最佳实践。
20	
21	---
22	
23	## 1. 工作模式
24	
25	开始前选择模式：
26	
27	| 模式 | 说明 | 适用 |
28	|------|------|------|
29	| **Build** | 从实验笔记/结果/代码生成论文 | 新稿 |
30	| **Improve** | 改写已有章节，强化论证 | 修改稿 |
31	| **Audit** | 输出风险列表 + 缺失证据 + 修复建议 | 投前检查 |
32	
33	---
34	
35	## 2. Claim-Evidence 方法论
36	
37	**核心原则：论文是一个有中心贡献的故事，不是实验的堆砌。**
38	
39	### 2.1 一句话贡献
40	
41	在写任何内容之前，必须能用一句话说清贡献。如果不能，说明还没准备好写论文。
42	
43	### 2.2 Claim-Evidence Map
44	
45	为每个 contribution 建立 claim→evidence 映射表：
46	
47	| Contribution | Claim | Evidence | Table/Figure |
48	|-------------|-------|----------|-------------|
49	| C1: 方法 X 在 Y 上 SOTA | 比所有 baseline 高 ≥2% | 5-seed 平均，p<0.05 | Table 1 |
50	| C2: 消融证明 Z 是关键 | 去掉 Z 后掉 >5% | 消融实验 | Table 2 |
51	| C3: 计算效率 | 比 baseline 快 3× | FLOPs + wall-clock | Figure 3 |
52	
53	**没有直接证据支撑的 claim 必须删除或降级为 discussion。**
54	
55	### 2.3 章节起草顺序
56	
57	```
58	1. Introduction + Experiments（先确定 claim 和 evidence）
59	2. Method（评估问题稳定后再写细节）
60	3. Related Work
61	4. Abstract + Title（核心 claim 定型后最后写）
62	```
63	
64	### 2.4 Quality Gates
65	
66	投稿前必须通过：
67	- [ ] 前两段出现显式 novelty 声明
68	- [ ] 每个 contribution 有可验证的 evidence
69	- [ ] Abstract / Intro / Conclusion 的 claim 一致
70	- [ ] Limitations 真实且技术性诚实
71	- [ ] 审稿人两分钟内能识别 delta
72	
73	---
74	
75	## 3. 引用防幻觉（CRITICAL）
76	
77	**AI 生成引用有 ~40% 错误率。绝对禁止凭记忆写 BibTeX。**
78	
79	### 3.1 黄金法则
80	
81	```
82	IF 无法程序化获取引用:
83	    → 标记 [CITATION NEEDED] 或 \cite{PLACEHOLDER_verify}
84	    → 明确告知用户
85	    → 绝不编造看似合理的引用
86	```
87	
88	### 3.2 五步验证流程
89	
90	```
91	1. SEARCH  → Semantic Scholar API 搜索关键词
92	2. VERIFY  → 至少 2 个来源确认论文存在（S2 + arXiv/CrossRef）
93	3. RETRIEVE → 通过 DOI 获取 BibTeX（程序化，非记忆）
94	4. CHECK   → 确认你引用的 claim 确实出自该论文
95	5. ADD     → 加入 .bib 文件
96	```
97	
98	### 3.3 API 速查
99	
100	| API | 用途 | 限制 |
101	|-----|------|------|
102	| **Semantic Scholar** | ML/AI 论文搜索 | 1 RPS (免费) |
103	| **CrossRef** | DOI → BibTeX | 需 mailto 头 |
104	| **arXiv** | 预印本搜索 | 3s 间隔 |
105	
106	```python
107	# DOI → BibTeX（最可靠的方式）
108	import requests
109	def doi_to_bibtex(doi: str) -> str:
110	    r = requests.get(f"https://doi.org/{doi}",
111	                     headers={"Accept": "application/x-bibtex"})
112	    r.raise_for_status()
113	    return r.text
114	
115	# Semantic Scholar 搜索
116	from semanticscholar import SemanticScholar
117	sch = SemanticScholar()
118	results = sch.search_paper("attention mechanism transformers", limit=5)
119	for p in results:
120	    print(f"{p.title} | DOI: {p.externalIds.get('DOI', 'N/A')}")
121	```
122	
123	### 3.4 引用处理规则
124	
125	| 情况 | 处理 |
126	|------|------|
127	| 找到论文 + DOI + BibTeX | 直接用 |
128	| 找到论文，无 DOI | 用 arXiv BibTeX |
129	| 论文存在但无法获取 BibTeX | 标记 placeholder，告知用户 |
130	| 不确定论文是否存在 | 标记 `[CITATION NEEDED]`，告知用户 |
131	| "我觉得有篇关于 X 的论文" | **绝不引用** — 先搜索或标记 |
132	
133	---
134	
135	## 4. 顶会模板速查
136	
137	### 4.1 ML/AI 会议
138	
139	| 会议 | 页数限制 | 主文件 | 样式文件 | 必须项 |
140	|------|---------|--------|---------|--------|
141	| **NeurIPS** | 9 页 | `main.tex` | `neurips.sty` | Paper Checklist |
142	| **ICML** | 8 页 (+1 camera-ready) | `example_paper.tex` | `icml2026.sty` | Broader Impact |
143	| **ICLR** | 9 页 (+1) | `iclr_conference.tex` | `iclr_conference.sty` | LLM 使用声明 |
144	| **ACL/EMNLP** | 8 页 (long) | `acl_latex.tex` | `acl.sty` | Limitations 必须 |
145	| **AAAI** | 7 页 (+1) | `aaai_template.tex` | `aaai.sty` | 严格样式 |
146	| **COLM** | 9 页 (+1) | `colm_conference.tex` | `colm_conference.sty` | 语言模型聚焦 |
147	
148	### 4.2 系统会议
149	
150	| 会议 | 页数限制 | 模板类型 | 关键要求 |
151	|------|---------|---------|---------|
152	| **OSDI** | 12 页 (+2) | USENIX `usenix.sty` | Research / Operational 双 track |
153	| **NSDI** | 12 页 | USENIX | Introduction 预筛 |
154	| **ASPLOS** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 前 2 页快速评审 |
155	| **SOSP** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 可选 Artifact Evaluation |
156	
157	### 4.3 模板使用原则
158	
159	```bash
160	# 1. 复制整个模板目录（不要只拷 .tex）
161	cp -r templates/neurips2025/ ~/papers/my-paper/
162	
163	# 2. 先编译未修改的模板，确认能跑通
164	latexmk -pdf main.tex
165	
166	# 3. 逐章替换内容，频繁编译
167	```
168	
169	**禁止事项：**
170	- 不要修改 `.sty` 文件
171	- 不要在会议模板间复制 `\usepackage` 行
172	- 不要只复制 `.tex` 而不带 `.sty/.bst`
173	
174	---
175	
176	## 5. 写作规范
177	
178	### 5.1 时间分配（Neel Nanda）
179	
180	花**大致相等**的时间在：
181	1. Abstract
182	2. Introduction
183	3. 图表
184	4. **其余所有内容加起来**
185	
186	审稿人读论文的顺序：标题 → 摘要 → 引言 → 图表 → 也许正文。
187	
188	### 5.2 Abstract 五句法（Sebastian Farquhar）
189	
190	```
191	1. 你做了什么（"We introduce/prove/demonstrate..."）
192	2. 为什么这很难且重要
193	3. 怎么做的（含专业关键词以便检索）
194	4. 有什么证据
195	5. 最惊人的数字/结果
196	```
197	
198	删除一切泛泛的开头：~~"Large language models have achieved remarkable success..."~~
199	
200	### 5.3 句子级清晰度（Gopen & Swan）
201	
202	| 原则 | 规则 |
203	|------|------|
204	| 主谓紧邻 | 不要在主语和动词之间插入长从句 |
205	| 重点在句尾 | 把关键数字/结论放在句末 |
206	| 旧信息在前 | 先放读者已知的内容，再引入新概念 |
207	| 动词表达动作 | "We analyzed" 而非 "We performed an analysis" |
208	
209	### 5.4 常见修改
210	
211	| 问题 | 修复 |
212	|------|------|
213	| Abstract 太泛 | 删第一句（如果它能放在任何 ML 论文前面） |
214	| Introduction 超 1.5 页 | 背景挪到 Related Work |
215	| 实验没有显式 claim | 每个实验前加 "This tests whether..." |
216	| 缺统计显著性 | 加 error bars + 运行次数 + 计算方法 |
217	
218	---
219	
220	## 6. 投稿工程链
221	
222	### 6.1 构建
223	
224	```bash
225	# 推荐：latexmk 一键构建
226	latexmk -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error main.tex
227	
228	# 手动：需要多次编译
229	pdflatex main.tex && bibtex main && pdflatex main.tex && pdflatex main.tex
230	```
231	
232	### 6.2 Lint + 格式化
233	
234	```bash
235	# Lint: 检查常见 LaTeX 问题
236	chktex main.tex
237	
238	# 格式化: 减少 diff 噪声
239	latexindent -w main.tex
240	```
241	
242	### 6.3 图表格式
243	
244	| 类型 | 格式 | 说明 |
245	|------|------|------|
246	| 矢量图（plot、diagram） | PDF | matplotlib: `plt.savefig('fig.pdf')` |
247	| 照片/heatmap | PNG 600dpi 或 TIFF | 栅格图 |
248	| 表格 | `booktabs` 包 | `\toprule/\midrule/\bottomrule` |
249	
250	```latex
251	\usepackage{booktabs}
252	\begin{tabular}{lcc}
253	\toprule
254	Method & Accuracy $\uparrow$ & Latency $\downarrow$ \\
255	\midrule
256	Baseline & 85.2 & 45ms \\
257	\textbf{Ours} & \textbf{92.1} & 38ms \\
258	\bottomrule
259	\end{tabular}
260	```
261	
262	**图表规范：**
263	- 用色盲友好色板（Okabe-Ito 或 Paul Tol）
264	- 图内不放标题（用 caption）
265	- Caption 独立可理解（不依赖正文）
266	- 最佳值加粗，标注方向符号（↑ 越高越好，↓ 越低越好）
267	
268	### 6.4 投稿打包
269	
270	```bash
271	# 清理辅助文件
272	latexmk -c
273	
274	# 打包投稿
275	zip -r submission.zip main.tex *.sty *.bst *.bib figures/ --exclude='*.aux' --exclude='*.log'
276	```
277	
278	### 6.5 常见失败点
279	
280	| 问题 | 解决 |
281	|------|------|
282	| 图片格式混用导致编译失败 | 统一用 PDF |
283	| 字体未嵌入 | `pdffonts output.pdf` 检查 |
284	| Overfull box 过多 | 关键位置手动调行 |
285	| 引用缺字段 | 检查 DOI/年份/期刊名 |
286	| 超页数 | 用 `\vspace{-Xpt}` 微调，或精简内容 |
287	
288	---
289	
290	## 7. 会议转投
291	
292	当论文被拒或转投其他会议时：
293	
294	### 7.1 ML/AI 会议间转换
295	
296	| 转换 | 页数变化 | 关键调整 |
297	|------|---------|---------|
298	| NeurIPS → ICML | 9→8 | 删 1 页，加 Broader Impact |
299	| ICML → ICLR | 8→9 | 可扩展实验 + LLM 声明 |
300	| NeurIPS → ACL | 9→8 | 按 NLP 惯例重组 + Limitations |
301	| ICLR → AAAI | 9→7 | 大幅精简，严格样式 |
302	
303	### 7.2 转投原则
304	
305	1. **永远用目标模板重新开始** — 复制目标模板，迁移内容，不要合并 preamble
306	2. **只迁移正文内容** — 不复制 `\usepackage`、header/footer 命令
307	3. **根据审稿意见改进** — 但不要在新稿中提及旧投稿（双盲）
308	4. **检查目标会议特殊要求** — checklist、ethics statement、LLM 声明等
309	
310	---
311	
312	## 8. 投前清单
313	
314	### 通用清单
315	
316	- [ ] Abstract/Intro/Conclusion 的 claim 一致
317	- [ ] 每个 contribution 有对应 evidence
318	- [ ] 所有引用已程序化验证（无幻觉引用）
319	- [ ] Error bars + 运行次数 + 统计方法
320	- [ ] Limitations 章节存在且诚实
321	- [ ] 匿名化（双盲审稿）
322	- [ ] 符合页数限制
323	- [ ] 所有图表有自包含 caption
324	- [ ] `.bib` 中无缺失字段
325	- [ ] PDF 编译无 warning
326	
327	### 会议特定
328	
329	| 会议 | 额外要求 |
330	|------|---------|
331	| NeurIPS | 16 项 Paper Checklist（附录，不计页数） |
332	| ICML | Broader Impact Statement |
333	| ICLR | LLM 使用声明 |
334	| ACL/EMNLP | Limitations 章节（必须），Ethics Statement |
335	| AAAI | 严格样式文件合规 |
336	
337	---
338	
339	## 参考资源
340	
341	**写作方法论：**
342	- [Neel Nanda: How to Write ML Papers](https://www.alignmentforum.org/posts/eJGptPbbFPZGLpjsp/) — What/Why/So What 框架
343	- [Farquhar: How to Write ML Papers](https://sebastianfarquhar.com/on-research/2024/11/04/how_to_write_ml_papers/) — 五句法 Abstract
344	- [Gopen & Swan: Science of Scientific Writing](https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~swanson/papers/science-of-writing.pdf) — 读者预期 7 原则
345	- [Lipton: Heuristics for Scientific Writing](https://www.approximatelycorrect.com/2018/01/29/heuristics-technical-scientific-writing-machine-learning-perspective/) — 用词
346	- [Perez: Easy Paper Writing Tips](https://ethanperez.net/easy-paper-writing-tips/) — 微观清晰度
347	
348	**API：**
349	- [Semantic Scholar](https://api.semanticscholar.org/api-docs/) | [CrossRef](https://www.crossref.org/documentation/) | [arXiv](https://info.arxiv.org/help/api/)
350	
351	**会议官方：**
352	- [NeurIPS](https://neurips.cc/) | [ICML](https://icml.cc/) | [ICLR](https://iclr.cc/) | [ACL](https://www.aclweb.org/) | [AAAI](https://aaai.org/) | [EMNLP](https://2025.emnlp.org/)

# LaTeX 论文写作全流程

ML/AI 顶会论文从草稿到投稿的完整指南。整合 Orchestra Research、VibeSkills、claim2evidence 三方最佳实践。

---

## 1. 工作模式

开始前选择模式：

| 模式 | 说明 | 适用 |
|------|------|------|
| **Build** | 从实验笔记/结果/代码生成论文 | 新稿 |
| **Improve** | 改写已有章节，强化论证 | 修改稿 |
| **Audit** | 输出风险列表 + 缺失证据 + 修复建议 | 投前检查 |

---

## 2. Claim-Evidence 方法论

**核心原则：论文是一个有中心贡献的故事，不是实验的堆砌。**

### 2.1 一句话贡献

在写任何内容之前，必须能用一句话说清贡献。如果不能，说明还没准备好写论文。

### 2.2 Claim-Evidence Map

为每个 contribution 建立 claim→evidence 映射表：

| Contribution | Claim | Evidence | Table/Figure |
|-------------|-------|----------|-------------|
| C1: 方法 X 在 Y 上 SOTA | 比所有 baseline 高 ≥2% | 5-seed 平均，p<0.05 | Table 1 |
| C2: 消融证明 Z 是关键 | 去掉 Z 后掉 >5% | 消融实验 | Table 2 |
| C3: 计算效率 | 比 baseline 快 3× | FLOPs + wall-clock | Figure 3 |

**没有直接证据支撑的 claim 必须删除或降级为 discussion。**

### 2.3 章节起草顺序

```
1. Introduction + Experiments（先确定 claim 和 evidence）
2. Method（评估问题稳定后再写细节）
3. Related Work
4. Abstract + Title（核心 claim 定型后最后写）
```

### 2.4 Quality Gates

投稿前必须通过：
- [ ] 前两段出现显式 novelty 声明
- [ ] 每个 contribution 有可验证的 evidence
- [ ] Abstract / Intro / Conclusion 的 claim 一致
- [ ] Limitations 真实且技术性诚实
- [ ] 审稿人两分钟内能识别 delta

---

## 3. 引用防幻觉（CRITICAL）

**AI 生成引用有 ~40% 错误率。绝对禁止凭记忆写 BibTeX。**

### 3.1 黄金法则

```
IF 无法程序化获取引用:
    → 标记 [CITATION NEEDED] 或 \cite{PLACEHOLDER_verify}
    → 明确告知用户
    → 绝不编造看似合理的引用
```

### 3.2 五步验证流程

```
1. SEARCH  → Semantic Scholar API 搜索关键词
2. VERIFY  → 至少 2 个来源确认论文存在（S2 + arXiv/CrossRef）
3. RETRIEVE → 通过 DOI 获取 BibTeX（程序化，非记忆）
4. CHECK   → 确认你引用的 claim 确实出自该论文
5. ADD     → 加入 .bib 文件
```

### 3.3 API 速查

| API | 用途 | 限制 |
|-----|------|------|
| **Semantic Scholar** | ML/AI 论文搜索 | 1 RPS (免费) |
| **CrossRef** | DOI → BibTeX | 需 mailto 头 |
| **arXiv** | 预印本搜索 | 3s 间隔 |

```python
# DOI → BibTeX（最可靠的方式）
import requests
def doi_to_bibtex(doi: str) -> str:
    r = requests.get(f"https://doi.org/{doi}",
                     headers={"Accept": "application/x-bibtex"})
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.text

# Semantic Scholar 搜索
from semanticscholar import SemanticScholar
sch = SemanticScholar()
results = sch.search_paper("attention mechanism transformers", limit=5)
for p in results:
    print(f"{p.title} | DOI: {p.externalIds.get('DOI', 'N/A')}")
```

### 3.4 引用处理规则

| 情况 | 处理 |
|------|------|
| 找到论文 + DOI + BibTeX | 直接用 |
| 找到论文，无 DOI | 用 arXiv BibTeX |
| 论文存在但无法获取 BibTeX | 标记 placeholder，告知用户 |
| 不确定论文是否存在 | 标记 `[CITATION NEEDED]`，告知用户 |
| "我觉得有篇关于 X 的论文" | **绝不引用** — 先搜索或标记 |

---

## 4. 顶会模板速查

### 4.1 ML/AI 会议

| 会议 | 页数限制 | 主文件 | 样式文件 | 必须项 |
|------|---------|--------|---------|--------|
| **NeurIPS** | 9 页 | `main.tex` | `neurips.sty` | Paper Checklist |
| **ICML** | 8 页 (+1 camera-ready) | `example_paper.tex` | `icml2026.sty` | Broader Impact |
| **ICLR** | 9 页 (+1) | `iclr_conference.tex` | `iclr_conference.sty` | LLM 使用声明 |
| **ACL/EMNLP** | 8 页 (long) | `acl_latex.tex` | `acl.sty` | Limitations 必须 |
| **AAAI** | 7 页 (+1) | `aaai_template.tex` | `aaai.sty` | 严格样式 |
| **COLM** | 9 页 (+1) | `colm_conference.tex` | `colm_conference.sty` | 语言模型聚焦 |

### 4.2 系统会议

| 会议 | 页数限制 | 模板类型 | 关键要求 |
|------|---------|---------|---------|
| **OSDI** | 12 页 (+2) | USENIX `usenix.sty` | Research / Operational 双 track |
| **NSDI** | 12 页 | USENIX | Introduction 预筛 |
| **ASPLOS** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 前 2 页快速评审 |
| **SOSP** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 可选 Artifact Evaluation |

### 4.3 模板使用原则

```bash
# 1. 复制整个模板目录（不要只拷 .tex）
cp -r templates/neurips2025/ ~/papers/my-paper/

# 2. 先编译未修改的模板，确认能跑通
latexmk -pdf main.tex

# 3. 逐章替换内容，频繁编译
```

**禁止事项：**
- 不要修改 `.sty` 文件
- 不要在会议模板间复制 `\usepackage` 行
- 不要只复制 `.tex` 而不带 `.sty/.bst`

---

## 5. 写作规范

### 5.1 时间分配（Neel Nanda）

花**大致相等**的时间在：
1. Abstract
2. Introduction
3. 图表
4. **其余所有内容加起来**

审稿人读论文的顺序：标题 → 摘要 → 引言 → 图表 → 也许正文。

### 5.2 Abstract 五句法（Sebastian Farquhar）

```
1. 你做了什么（"We introduce/prove/demonstrate..."）
2. 为什么这很难且重要
3. 怎么做的（含专业关键词以便检索）
4. 有什么证据
5. 最惊人的数字/结果
```

删除一切泛泛的开头：~~"Large language models have achieved remarkable success..."~~

### 5.3 句子级清晰度（Gopen & Swan）

| 原则 | 规则 |
|------|------|
| 主谓紧邻 | 不要在主语和动词之间插入长从句 |
| 重点在句尾 | 把关键数字/结论放在句末 |
| 旧信息在前 | 先放读者已知的内容，再引入新概念 |
| 动词表达动作 | "We analyzed" 而非 "We performed an analysis" |

### 5.4 常见修改

| 问题 | 修复 |
|------|------|
| Abstract 太泛 | 删第一句（如果它能放在任何 ML 论文前面） |
| Introduction 超 1.5 页 | 背景挪到 Related Work |
| 实验没有显式 claim | 每个实验前加 "This tests whether..." |
| 缺统计显著性 | 加 error bars + 运行次数 + 计算方法 |

---

## 6. 投稿工程链

### 6.1 构建

```bash
# 推荐：latexmk 一键构建
latexmk -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error main.tex

# 手动：需要多次编译
pdflatex main.tex && bibtex main && pdflatex main.tex && pdflatex main.tex
```

### 6.2 Lint + 格式化

```bash
# Lint: 检查常见 LaTeX 问题
chktex main.tex

# 格式化: 减少 diff 噪声
latexindent -w main.tex
```

### 6.3 图表格式

| 类型 | 格式 | 说明 |
|------|------|------|
| 矢量图（plot、diagram） | PDF | matplotlib: `plt.savefig('fig.pdf')` |
| 照片/heatmap | PNG 600dpi 或 TIFF | 栅格图 |
| 表格 | `booktabs` 包 | `\toprule/\midrule/\bottomrule` |

```latex
\usepackage{booktabs}
\begin{tabular}{lcc}
\toprule
Method & Accuracy $\uparrow$ & Latency $\downarrow$ \\
\midrule
Baseline & 85.2 & 45ms \\
\textbf{Ours} & \textbf{92.1} & 38ms \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
```

**图表规范：**
- 用色盲友好色板（Okabe-Ito 或 Paul Tol）
- 图内不放标题（用 caption）
- Caption 独立可理解（不依赖正文）
- 最佳值加粗，标注方向符号（↑ 越高越好，↓ 越低越好）

### 6.4 投稿打包

```bash
# 清理辅助文件
latexmk -c

# 打包投稿
zip -r submission.zip main.tex *.sty *.bst *.bib figures/ --exclude='*.aux' --exclude='*.log'
```

### 6.5 常见失败点

| 问题 | 解决 |
|------|------|
| 图片格式混用导致编译失败 | 统一用 PDF |
| 字体未嵌入 | `pdffonts output.pdf` 检查 |
| Overfull box 过多 | 关键位置手动调行 |
| 引用缺字段 | 检查 DOI/年份/期刊名 |
| 超页数 | 用 `\vspace{-Xpt}` 微调，或精简内容 |

---

## 7. 会议转投

当论文被拒或转投其他会议时：

### 7.1 ML/AI 会议间转换

| 转换 | 页数变化 | 关键调整 |
|------|---------|---------|
| NeurIPS → ICML | 9→8 | 删 1 页，加 Broader Impact |
| ICML → ICLR | 8→9 | 可扩展实验 + LLM 声明 |
| NeurIPS → ACL | 9→8 | 按 NLP 惯例重组 + Limitations |
| ICLR → AAAI | 9→7 | 大幅精简，严格样式 |

### 7.2 转投原则

1. **永远用目标模板重新开始** — 复制目标模板，迁移内容，不要合并 preamble
2. **只迁移正文内容** — 不复制 `\usepackage`、header/footer 命令
3. **根据审稿意见改进** — 但不要在新稿中提及旧投稿（双盲）
4. **检查目标会议特殊要求** — checklist、ethics statement、LLM 声明等

---

## 8. 投前清单

### 通用清单

- [ ] Abstract/Intro/Conclusion 的 claim 一致
- [ ] 每个 contribution 有对应 evidence
- [ ] 所有引用已程序化验证（无幻觉引用）
- [ ] Error bars + 运行次数 + 统计方法
- [ ] Limitations 章节存在且诚实
- [ ] 匿名化（双盲审稿）
- [ ] 符合页数限制
- [ ] 所有图表有自包含 caption
- [ ] `.bib` 中无缺失字段
- [ ] PDF 编译无 warning

### 会议特定

| 会议 | 额外要求 |
|------|---------|
| NeurIPS | 16 项 Paper Checklist（附录，不计页数） |
| ICML | Broader Impact Statement |
| ICLR | LLM 使用声明 |
| ACL/EMNLP | Limitations 章节（必须），Ethics Statement |
| AAAI | 严格样式文件合规 |

---

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

Per-head mixed-precision quantization of the KV cache is a natural strategy for reducing memory during LLM inference: assign fewer bits to insensitive heads and more bits to sensitive ones, achieving lower perplexity than uniform quantization at the same average bit-width.
Recent work on KV cache quantization explores both uniform schemes~\cite{liu2024kivi,hooper2024kvquant,lin2024qserve,he2024zipcache} and token-level mixed-precision approaches~\cite{ge2024fastgen,lei2026arkv}, while complementary methods reduce cache size through eviction~\cite{zhang2023h2o,li2024snapkv}.
RateQuant~\cite{zuo2026ratequant} formalizes per-head allocation as a rate-distortion optimization and shows that greedy allocation is optimal when bit-widths are consecutive integers $\{2,3,4,5,6\}$, exploiting the polymatroid structure of the feasible set (their Proposition~6).

In practice, hardware-efficient inference requires bit-widths drawn from $\{2, 4, 8, 16\}$---the formats natively supported by modern accelerators.
On this non-consecutive set, the polymatroid structure breaks down, and greedy is no longer provably optimal.
One might expect that exact MCKP solvers would fill this gap.
They do not.
On Qwen2.5-7B at $4\times$ compression, unconstrained greedy achieves 32.45 PPL and unconstrained MCKP achieves 36.92---both \emph{far worse} than uniform 4-bit (15.45).
The optimization does not merely underperform; it fails catastrophically.

The root cause is not solver suboptimality but a violation of the objective's additive distortion assumption.
Both solvers assign 68--75 of 112 KV heads to 2-bit, where per-head quantization errors are large enough to compound through the residual stream.
The additive model predicts $\sim$11 PPL for these allocations; the actual PPL is $3$--$4\times$ higher.
At 4-bit and above, per-head distortions are small and compound negligibly---uniform 4-bit achieves close to its additive prediction---but 2-bit distortions are orders of magnitude larger.
When most heads are quantized to 2-bit simultaneously, cumulative truncation errors exceed the network's capacity to compensate, and perplexity degrades super-linearly.

This observation points to a minimal intervention: cap the number of 2-bit assignments.
We add a single cardinality constraint $\sum_h \mathbb{1}[b_h{=}2] \leq k$ to the standard MCKP formulation (\S\ref{sec:method}).
On Qwen2.5-7B, setting $k{=}8$ (7\% of heads) yields 11.23 PPL---a 27.3\% reduction over uniform 4-bit.
The constraint works by forcing the solver to use 2-bit only on the least-sensitive heads, while redistributing the freed budget to protect sensitive heads at 8-bit or 16-bit.
This is not a heuristic patch: the constraint directly addresses the identified failure mode and is compatible with any solver.

A surprising consequence is that, under the cardinality constraint, the choice of solver becomes irrelevant.
Constrained greedy and constrained MCKP produce identical allocations---not approximately, but exactly: all 112 heads receive the same bit-width on Qwen2.5-7B, all 256 on Llama-3.1-8B, and 255 of 256 on Mistral-7B-v0.3 (the single difference is a zero-distortion tie with no PPL impact).
The constraint narrows the feasible set enough that greedy's locally optimal decisions are globally optimal (\S\ref{sec:solver_equiv}), enabling practitioners to use the simpler $O(H \log H)$ greedy algorithm without sacrificing solution quality.

However, non-uniform allocation does not help universally.
On Llama-3.1-8B, constrained MCKP achieves 8.45 PPL vs.\ uniform 8.47---a marginal 0.2\% improvement.
On Mistral-7B-v0.3, it is slightly \emph{worse}: 7.16 vs.\ 7.13.
The difference across architectures traces to head sensitivity heterogeneity: Qwen's KV heads vary widely in 2-bit distortion, with Layer-0 heads contributing a disproportionate share, while Mistral's heads are nearly uniform in sensitivity.
When there is no heterogeneity to exploit, non-uniform allocation adds noise without benefit.

This motivates a diagnostic question that prior work does not address: \emph{when} should a practitioner use per-head mixed-precision quantization?
We propose a heterogeneity diagnostic based on the top-5\% concentration of per-head distortion (\S\ref{sec:heterogeneity}).
On our three architectures, the metric cleanly separates the beneficial case (Qwen, concentration 0.59--0.66, 27.3\% PPL improvement) from the neutral case (Llama, 0.34--0.59, marginal) and the counterproductive case (Mistral, 0.42, slightly worse than uniform).
The diagnostic reuses profiling data already required by the solver and adds no computational overhead.

Our contributions are:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep]
\item We identify 2-bit distortion compounding as the cause of catastrophic failure in unconstrained per-head KV cache quantization on hardware-aligned bit-widths, and show that a cardinality constraint on 2-bit assignments is a minimal sufficient fix, reducing Qwen2.5-7B PPL from 32--37 (unconstrained) to 11.23 (constrained) at $4\times$ compression (\S\ref{sec:compounding}, \S\ref{sec:experiments}).

\item We demonstrate that the cardinality constraint makes solver choice irrelevant: constrained greedy and constrained MCKP produce identical per-head allocations across three architectures, enabling use of a simple greedy algorithm (\S\ref{sec:solver_equiv}).

\item We propose a heterogeneity-based diagnostic framework that predicts whether non-uniform allocation will help a given architecture, validated on three models spanning beneficial, marginal, and counterproductive outcomes (\S\ref{sec:heterogeneity}).
\end{enumerate}

1	\section{Method}
2	\label{sec:method}
3	
4	\subsection{Problem Formulation}
5	\label{sec:formulation}
6	
7	We formulate per-head KV cache quantization as a constrained optimization problem.
8	Let $h \in \{1,\ldots,H\}$ index the KV heads across all layers, $b_h \in \mathcal{B}$ the bit-width assigned to head $h$, and $\mathcal{B} = \{2, 4, 8, 16\}$ the set of hardware-aligned bit-widths.
9	Each head $h$ has a profiled distortion function $d_h(b)$, the PPL increase when head $h$ is quantized to $b$ bits.
10	Given a memory budget ratio $R$ (e.g., $R = 0.25$ for $4\times$ compression), we seek the allocation that minimizes total distortion:
11	\begin{equation}
12	\label{eq:objective}
13	\min_{\{b_h\}} \sum_{h=1}^{H} d_h(b_h) \quad \text{s.t.} \quad \frac{1}{H \cdot 16}\sum_{h=1}^{H} b_h \leq R.
14	\end{equation}
15	
16	This is a multiple-choice knapsack problem (MCKP): each head selects one bit-width from $\mathcal{B}$ to minimize total distortion under a budget.
17	RateQuant~\cite{zuo2026ratequant} solves this for consecutive bit-widths $\{2,3,4,5,6\}$, where the polymatroid structure of the feasible set guarantees that greedy allocation is optimal (their Proposition 6).
18	Hardware-aligned bit-widths $\{2,4,8,16\}$ are non-consecutive; the gaps break this structure, and greedy is no longer guaranteed to match the MCKP optimum.
19	Moreover, as we show in \S\ref{sec:compounding}, the objective itself is not well-behaved: distortions from 2-bit heads compound non-additively, making unconstrained optimization unreliable.
20	
21	\subsection{PPL-based Per-Head Profiling}
22	\label{sec:profiling}
23	
24	We profile each KV head independently by quantizing it to each $b \in \mathcal{B}$ while keeping all other heads at bf16, and measuring the resulting PPL increase $d_h(b)$ on a calibration set of 64 sequences $\times$ 2048 tokens from WikiText-2 train.
25	This yields a distortion table of $H \times |\mathcal{B}|$ entries that serves as input to the solver.
26	
27	The optimization in Eq.~\eqref{eq:objective} relies on an additive distortion assumption: the total PPL degradation from a mixed-precision allocation is approximately $\sum_h d_h(b_h)$.
28	This holds when per-head distortions are small and independent---a reasonable approximation for 4-bit and 8-bit quantization, where individual head distortions are typically below 0.1 PPL.
29	At 2-bit, however, individual distortions are orders of magnitude larger, and the additive assumption breaks down.
30	
31	\subsection{Compounding Effect}
32	\label{sec:compounding}
33	
34	When many heads are simultaneously quantized to 2-bit, per-head distortions compound non-additively.
35	The mechanism is straightforward: each head's quantized output feeds into the residual stream, and truncation errors from multiple 2-bit heads accumulate through subsequent layers.
36	When the number of 2-bit heads is small, these errors are absorbed by the remaining high-precision heads.
37	As the count grows, cumulative errors exceed the capacity of the residual stream to compensate, and PPL degrades super-linearly.
38	
39	\begin{figure}[t]
40	\centering
41	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/fig2_compounding_curve.pdf}
42	\caption{PPL on Qwen2.5-7B ($4\times$ compression) as a function of $k$, the maximum number of 2-bit heads. Too few 2-bit heads waste budget on 4-bit; too many trigger compounding. The minimum occurs at $k{=}8$.}
43	\label{fig:compounding}
44	\end{figure}
45	
46	Unconstrained solvers are blind to this effect because the additive objective underestimates the cost of large-scale 2-bit assignment.
47	On Qwen2.5-7B, unconstrained greedy assigns 68 heads to 2-bit and achieves 32.45 PPL; unconstrained MCKP assigns 75 heads and achieves 36.92---both far worse than uniform 4-bit (15.45).
48	The additive model predicts $\sim$11 PPL for these allocations, underestimating the actual degradation by $3\text{--}4\times$.
49	
50	This compounding is specific to 2-bit quantization.
51	At 4-bit and above, per-head distortions are small enough that additivity holds even when all heads share the same bit-width (uniform 4-bit achieves 15.45 PPL, close to the sum-of-distortions prediction).
52	The qualitative difference arises because 2-bit quantization has far larger per-head distortion, saturating the error tolerance of the residual stream.
53	
54	Figure~\ref{fig:compounding} shows the relationship between $k$ (the maximum number of 2-bit heads) and PPL on Qwen2.5-7B at $4\times$ compression.
55	The curve is U-shaped: at $k{=}0$ (uniform 4-bit), PPL is 15.45; allowing a few 2-bit heads reduces PPL by freeing budget for 8-bit heads on sensitive positions, reaching a minimum of 11.23 at $k{=}8$; beyond this point, compounding drives PPL upward, reaching 35.35 at $k{=}75$.
56	
57	\subsection{Cardinality Constraint}
58	\label{sec:cardinality}
59	
60	The compounding effect motivates a simple addition to Eq.~\eqref{eq:objective}: a cardinality constraint on 2-bit assignments.
61	\begin{equation}
62	\label{eq:constraint}
63	\sum_{h=1}^{H} \mathbb{1}[b_h = 2] \leq k.
64	\end{equation}
65	
66	The constraint parameter $k$ is selected by a small-scale sweep on calibration data: solve the constrained problem for each candidate $k$, evaluate calibration PPL, and pick the value at the minimum of the U-shaped curve (Figure~\ref{fig:compounding}).
67	For Qwen2.5-7B with 112 KV heads, $k{=}8$ ($\sim$7\% of heads).
68	
69	The constraint is a single linear inequality, compatible with any solver---greedy, MCKP, or integer linear programming---and adds negligible overhead to the optimization.
70	
71	A natural question is whether Layer-0 heads require explicit protection, since attention heads in the first layer are known to carry disproportionate importance.
72	On Qwen2.5-7B, the profiler assigns very high distortion to Layer-0 heads (e.g., L0H0: $+$31.9\%, L0H2: $+$23.2\%, L0H3: $+$11.7\% PPL increase at 2-bit).
73	These values are large enough that no solver would assign 2-bit to Layer-0 under any reasonable budget.
74	We verify this empirically: running the solver with and without manual Layer-0 exclusion produces identical allocations across all 112 heads.
75	No manual exclusion rule is needed; the profiler signal is sufficient.
76	
77	\subsection{Solver Equivalence}
78	\label{sec:solver_equiv}
79	
80	\begin{table}[t]
81	\centering
82	\small
83	\caption{Solver comparison on Qwen2.5-7B at $4\times$ compression. Unconstrained solvers over-allocate 2-bit heads and fail catastrophically. The cardinality constraint ($k{\leq}8$) makes greedy and MCKP produce identical allocations.\footnotemark}
84	\label{tab:solver_equiv}
85	\begin{tabular}{llcccc}
86	\toprule
87	Solver & Constraint & PPL & \multicolumn{3}{c}{Bit distribution} \\
88	 & & & 2-bit & 4-bit & 8/16-bit \\
89	\midrule
90	Greedy & None & 32.45 & 68 & 30 & 14 \\
91	MCKP & None & 36.92 & 75 & 33 & 4 \\
92	Greedy & $k{\leq}8$ & 11.23 & 8 & 100 & 4 \\
93	MCKP & $k{\leq}8$ & 11.23 & 8 & 100 & 4 \\
94	Uniform & --- & 15.45 & 0 & 112 & 0 \\
95	\bottomrule
96	\end{tabular}
97	\end{table}
98	\footnotetext{Standard-resolution profiling; hires profiling (64 seq $\times$ 2048 tok) achieves 10.91 (\S\ref{sec:profiling_resolution}).}
99	
100	With the cardinality constraint in place, greedy and MCKP produce identical results---not approximately, but exactly.
101	Table~\ref{tab:solver_equiv} shows that constrained greedy and constrained MCKP achieve the same PPL (11.23) with the same bit distribution on Qwen2.5-7B.
102	We verify this at the per-head level across three models:
103	
104	\begin{itemize}[nosep]
105	\item \textbf{Qwen2.5-7B:} 112/112 heads receive identical bit-widths.
106	\item \textbf{Llama-3.1-8B:} 256/256 heads identical.
107	\item \textbf{Mistral-7B-v0.3:} 255/256 heads identical. The single difference is a zero-distortion tie between two heads at 4-bit and 8-bit, with no PPL impact.
108	\end{itemize}
109	
110	The constraint narrows the feasible set enough that greedy's locally optimal decisions are globally optimal.
111	Without it, greedy cascades into excessive 2-bit allocation: each additional 2-bit head looks locally beneficial (freeing budget) but contributes to the compounding effect that degrades global PPL.
112	The cardinality constraint breaks this cascade by capping the number of 2-bit heads, aligning local and global optima.
113	
114	The practical implication is that practitioners can use the simpler $O(H \log H)$ greedy algorithm instead of MCKP without sacrificing optimality.

\section{Related Work}\label{sec:related_work}

\paragraph{KV Cache Quantization.}
Several methods quantize the KV cache at a uniform bit-width.
KIVI~\cite{liu2024kivi} applies asymmetric 2-bit quantization per channel for keys and per token for values.
KVQuant~\cite{hooper2024kvquant} extends this to ultra-long contexts with per-channel sensitivity-weighted rounding.
QServe~\cite{lin2024qserve} co-designs W4A8KV4 quantization with a serving system for end-to-end speedup.
ZipCache~\cite{he2024zipcache} identifies salient tokens and quantizes them at higher precision while compressing the rest.
GEAR~\cite{kang2024gear} combines low-rank approximation with sparse residual correction to achieve near-lossless compression.
SKVQ~\cite{duanmu2024skvq} introduces sliding-window quantization that adapts to the recency structure of attention.
These methods apply a single bit-width across all heads (or all tokens within a head).
We extend the design space to per-head non-uniform allocation over the hardware-aligned action set $\{2,4,8,16\}$, and study the conditions under which this additional flexibility is beneficial.

\paragraph{KV Cache Eviction.}
An orthogonal line of work reduces cache size by evicting tokens rather than compressing them.
H2O~\cite{zhang2023h2o} retains only ``heavy-hitter'' tokens that accumulate large attention mass.
SnapKV~\cite{li2024snapkv} selects important tokens per head via an observation window before generation begins.
FastGen~\cite{ge2024fastgen} applies per-head adaptive policies---some heads retain all tokens, others keep only recent or attention-heavy ones.
Scissorhands~\cite{liu2024scissorhands} exploits the persistence of token importance across decoding steps to prune once and reuse.
StreamingLLM~\cite{xiao2024streamingllm} maintains a fixed-size cache of attention sinks plus a sliding window for unbounded-length generation.
PyramidInfer~\cite{yang2024pyramidinfer} progressively reduces cache across layers, retaining more tokens in lower layers.
These eviction strategies are complementary to quantization: one can first evict unimportant tokens, then quantize the retained cache.
Our work focuses exclusively on the quantization allocation problem.

\paragraph{Mixed-Precision Rate-Distortion Allocation.}
The closest line of work formulates non-uniform KV cache quantization as rate-distortion optimization.
RateQuant~\cite{zuo2026ratequant} casts per-head bit-width selection as a multiple-choice knapsack problem and proves that greedy allocation is optimal when bit-widths are consecutive integers $\{2,\ldots,6\}$, exploiting the polymatroid structure of the feasible set (their Proposition~6).
On hardware-aligned bit-widths $\{2,4,8,16\}$, the gaps between adjacent options break this structure, and greedy optimality no longer holds.
More critically, we show that unconstrained solvers---greedy or exact---fail catastrophically on this action set due to 2-bit distortion compounding, a failure mode that RateQuant's consecutive-integer setting does not encounter.
Our cardinality constraint addresses this compounding directly, and our heterogeneity diagnostic determines when non-uniform allocation is worthwhile.
SqueezeLLM~\cite{kim2024squeezellm} applies dense-and-sparse decomposition for weight quantization with sensitivity-based non-uniform precision, though at the weight rather than KV cache level.
ARKV~\cite{lei2026arkv} manages KV cache resources adaptively under memory budgets, operating at a coarser granularity than per-head allocation.
KVmix~\cite{li2025kvmix} uses gradient-based signals to assign mixed precision at the layer level rather than the head level, a complementary granularity to our per-head analysis.
MixKVQ~\cite{zhang2025mixkvq} introduces query-aware dynamic mixed precision that adjusts bit-widths at inference time; in contrast, our allocation is static, determined once during offline profiling and fixed thereafter.

\paragraph{Attention Head Analysis.}
Prior work has studied the functional roles and varying importance of individual attention heads, including analyses of head redundancy and pruning potential [UNVERIFIED: Voita et~al.\@ 2019] and the effect of removing heads on downstream task performance [UNVERIFIED: Michel et~al.\@ 2019].
These studies focus on which heads can be removed entirely.
Our analysis addresses a different question: which heads are sensitive to \emph{quantization}, and how heterogeneous that sensitivity is across architectures.
The heterogeneity diagnostic we propose (\S\ref{sec:heterogeneity}) measures concentration of per-head quantization distortion, not head importance for task accuracy---a phenomenon that, as our experiments show, varies substantially across model families and determines whether non-uniform allocation is beneficial.

GEAR~\cite{kang2024gear} combines low-rank approximation with sparse residual correction to achieve near-lossless compression.
SKVQ~\cite{duanmu2024skvq} introduces sliding-window quantization that adapts to the recency structure of attention.
These methods apply a single bit-width across all heads (or all tokens within a head).
We extend the design space to per-head non-uniform allocation over the hardware-aligned action set $\{2,4,8,16\}$, and study the conditions under which this additional flexibility is beneficial.

\paragraph{KV Cache Eviction.}
An orthogonal line of work reduces cache size by evicting tokens rather than compressing them.
H2O~\cite{zhang2023h2o} retains only ``heavy-hitter'' tokens that accumulate large attention mass.
SnapKV~\cite{li2024snapkv} selects important tokens per head via an observation window before generation begins.
FastGen~\cite{ge2024fastgen} applies per-head adaptive policies---some heads retain all tokens, others keep only recent or attention-heavy ones.
Scissorhands~\cite{liu2024scissorhands} exploits the persistence of token importance across decoding steps to prune once and reuse.
StreamingLLM~\cite{xiao2024streamingllm} maintains a fixed-size cache of attention sinks plus a sliding window for unbounded-length generation.
PyramidInfer~\cite{yang2024pyramidinfer} progressively reduces cache across layers, retaining more tokens in lower layers.
These eviction strategies are complementary to quantization: one can first evict unimportant tokens, then quantize the retained cache.
Our work focuses exclusively on the quantization allocation problem.

\paragraph{Mixed-Precision Rate-Distortion Allocation.}
The closest line of work formulates non-uniform KV cache quantization as rate-distortion optimization.
RateQuant~\cite{zuo2026ratequant} casts per-head bit-width selection as a multiple-choice knapsack problem and proves that greedy allocation is optimal when bit-widths are consecutive integers $\{2,\ldots,6\}$, exploiting the polymatroid structure of the feasible set (their Proposition~6).
On hardware-aligned bit-widths $\{2,4,8,16\}$, the gaps between adjacent options break this structure, and greedy optimality no longer holds.
More critically, we show that unconstrained solvers---greedy or exact---fail catastrophically on this action set due to 2-bit distortion compounding, a failure mode that RateQuant's consecutive-integer setting does not encounter.
Our cardinality constraint addresses this compounding directly, and our heterogeneity diagnostic determines when non-uniform allocation is worthwhile.
SqueezeLLM~\cite{kim2024squeezellm} applies dense-and-sparse decomposition for weight quantization with sensitivity-based non-uniform precision, though at the weight rather than KV cache level.
ARKV~\cite{lei2026arkv} manages KV cache resources adaptively under memory budgets, operating at a coarser granularity than per-head allocation.
KVmix~\cite{li2025kvmix} uses gradient-based signals to assign mixed precision at the layer level rather than the head level, a complementary granularity to our per-head analysis.
MixKVQ~\cite{zhang2025mixkvq} introduces query-aware dynamic mixed precision that adjusts bit-widths at inference time; in contrast, our allocation is static, determined once during offline profiling and fixed thereafter.

\paragraph{Attention Head Analysis.}
Prior work has studied the functional roles and varying importance of individual attention heads, including analyses of head redundancy and pruning potential [UNVERIFIED: Voita et~al.\@ 2019] and the effect of removing heads on downstream task performance [UNVERIFIED: Michel et~al.\@ 2019].
These studies focus on which heads can be removed entirely.
Our analysis addresses a different question: which heads are sensitive to \emph{quantization}, and how heterogeneous that sensitivity is across architectures.
The heterogeneity diagnostic we propose (\S\ref{sec:heterogeneity}) measures concentration of per-head quantization distortion, not head importance for task accuracy---a phenomenon that, as our experiments show, varies substantially across model families and determines whether non-uniform allocation is beneficial.
